To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

toluene potentiates P2X2, P2X4, P2X2/6 and P2X4/6 receptor-mediated currents at submaximal concentrations of ATP, but inhibits P2X3 and P2X2/P2X3 receptor-mediated currents at both low and maximal ATP concentrations.
the abused solvent, toluene, potentiates P2X receptor-mediated responses at concentrations that are within the range of those that have been reported to occur in the blood of toluene abusers.
toluene is able to potentiate P2X2, P2X4, P2X2/6, and P2X4/6 receptor currents, while inhibiting P2X3 currents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of toluene on the function of P(2X) receptors.
the mechanisms underlying the actions of abused substances.
the effects of the abused solvent, toluene, on the function of recombinant P(2X) receptor subunits and heteromers expressed in HEK-293 cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
toluene is an allosteric modulator of P2X receptor function.
the solvent toluene has the potential to affect the function of P(2X) receptors in a sub-unit and agonist specific manner.
the abused solvent, toluene, affects the function of recombinant P-2-X receptors in a sub-unit dependent and agonist dependent fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
toluene is an agonist of P2X4, P2X2/P2X4 and a weak inhibitor of P2X3 receptors.
the abused drug toluene potentiates P2X receptor function, and that these effects may be relevant to the effects of this solvent on the central nervous system.
toluene can affect the function of P 2X receptors in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
toluene is a positive allosteric modulator of ATP-gated currents through homomeric P4X4 and P4X2 receptors and heteromeric receptors containing both P2X6 and P2X4 or P2X3.
the abused solvent, toluene, affects the function of the P2X receptor in a subunit and concentration-dependent manner.
the abused drug, toluene, affects the function of certain P2X receptors, but not all.
